svg.title: Kurose's Pythagorean theorem (4.29), checked
svg.desc: Left: for random triples on the three-outcome simplex with orthogonal geodesics, the relative miss of the plain Pythagorean identity equals minus the predicted correction (one minus alpha squared) over 4 times D[p:q] D[q:r] / D[p:r], so all points lie on the line y = minus x. Right: the largest error of the plain sum and of the corrected formula against alpha, on a log scale: the corrected formula is exact to rounding, the plain sum is off except at alpha = plus or minus 1.
svg.text: log₁₀ of the largest error over 200 triples
Error of the plain sum and of (4.29)
Left: every random triple (the α-geodesic p→q orthogonal to the −α-geodesic q→r) lies on the line y = −x.
Right: with the correction the error is rounding (10⁻¹⁵); without it the miss reaches about 10⁻¹ for α = 3.
At α = ±1 both are exact (the floor of the plot is 10⁻¹⁶).
